definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carry from place to place
second meaning: to fill with rapture, carry away with joy

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to carry goods or people, and also to enrapture someone, sweeping them away emotionally.

clue.text: Being no longer in credit, Edward is worried

parts.note: a concern is a business, an entity in its own right
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is fretting because his account has slipped into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: A concern is a business or firm; the setter's 'no longer in credit' adds colour rather than letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone concerned is anxious or troubled about a matter.

clue.text: Give one the pip, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a pip is a seed of a fruit

explanation.surface: Annoy somebody, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone the pip is British slang for irritating them; here the pip is just a fruit seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or yield something, such as territory, to another.

clue.text: Tried saving the wherewithal for publishing

parts.words: Tried saving the wherewithal for publishing
parts.note: surface reading: someone tried to put money aside to fund a publication
setter's reading: the means of making something public, of publicising a product

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to save up the funds to publish a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'publishing' suggests books; read as making public, its means is the trade of promotion. The opening 'Tried saving' resists a clean parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising is the means by which goods and messages are made widely known to the public.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to express or declare

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example'; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: State means ceremonial grandeur, as in a state occasion, and as a verb means to declare.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to direct something at a target
second meaning: a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Advice to go for a headshot.
explanation.definitionFit: To point is to aim, and a point is a promontory or headland on a coast.

clue.text: Stable worker — he's just got married

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who looks after horses
second meaning: the man at the altar, short for bridegroom

explanation.surface: A stablehand has just tied the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a person who tends horses and a newly married man, the bridegroom.

indicators.note: turning something over and over changes its arrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it looks like a link but its letters are needed

explanation.surface: A moral: pride turns into a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like the joint of the proverb pride comes before a fall, but its four letters join the five of pride in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdition is ruin or damnation, an utter downfall, especially of the soul.

clue.text: Fire about a quarter, which is really not a lot

definitions.note: a noun: a small meal, not a lot of food

indicators.note: one word stands about the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
north, one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Dismissing someone over a measly quarter, which is hardly a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' suggests money or a fraction; here it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack is a light bite between meals, a small amount of food rather than a full spread.

clue.text: Once again showing the traveller as a consumer

parts.note: a commercial traveller, a sales representative
one consuming food is eating

explanation.surface: A programme re-running that casts the travelling salesman as a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep was the old name for a commercial traveller, a salesman on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast being repeated is being shown on screen for a second time.

clue.text: Broke with following in very short time

parts.note: split, past tense, means broke apart
second means coming next, following on

explanation.surface: Someone broke with their followers almost instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts in the reading, and 'Broke' tempts as meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is an instant, a tiny fraction of a moment.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: suitable, as an adjective

definitions.note: the verb: 'this' is the answer, which means to take
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the verb for seizing something for oneself

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective (stress on the last syllable but one) means suitable; the verb, spelt the same, means to take possession.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means suitable or proper; the verb means to seize something for one's own use.

clue.text: A gentleman of leisure may well get riled

indicators.note: may well get suggests turning into something else, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man of leisure is likely to become irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler does no work, so a gentleman of leisure is a polite description of one.

clue.text: Game it's wrong to make money on

parts.note: bad means wrong or wicked
to mint is to produce coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game on which gambling is immoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: makes amends or compensation for a wrong
second meaning: ..., puts on different clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as re-dresses: dresses again, in fresh clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or compensate for it; to re-dress is to change outfits.

parts.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A monk praises a fine cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' looks like the start of an exclamation; read as that is it becomes the abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's-milk cheese with a white rind.

indicators.note: perhaps says this is only one possible arrangement, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone landing one fewer, maybe a catch or a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lands' reads as a verb; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Isles are islands, pieces of land surrounded by water.

parts.note: taken as written
a bet is a chance or gamble

explanation.surface: An opportunity to give someone a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so to back someone up.

clue.text: Scientist's MS are torn, so must be repaired

definitions.note: the answer is plural, so read it as scientists

indicators.note: something torn that must be repaired has to be put back together in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, MS meaning manuscript

explanation.surface: A scientist's manuscripts have been ripped and need mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are part of the mix; the signal is 'must be repaired'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers are scientists who study stars, planets and the wider universe.

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a fresh sequence

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Snub her, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut her' suggests ignoring someone socially; 'Cut' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to cut, as with wool from a sheep or hair with large scissors.

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
ripe means fully mature

explanation.surface: A young grouse begins to come of age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' seems to be the game bird; it is the verb or noun for complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a complaint, and to grouse is to grumble, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Figure maybe he's an unusual guy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a written symbol, such as a digit or letter
second meaning: an eccentric person, a real one-off

explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks a figure as one example of the symbol sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a printed symbol, a numeral being one kind, and also an eccentric person.

parts.note: Eve, a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone forever correcting a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always or at all times, as in for ever.

clue.text: In time someone will design a shed to snap together

parts.note: surface padding that sets the scene and gives no letters

indicators.note: in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: found spanning these words: letters 5-9 of 'design a shed'

explanation.surface: Eventually someone will plan a flat-pack shed that clicks together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time someone will' is padding for the surface; the answer sits across 'design a shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind or snap the teeth together, often in anger.

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the sign for a parking place
to enter is to record, as in a register

explanation.surface: A dealer setting a record for parking his van.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled tradesman who works with wood.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to frown or scowl, also spelt lour
second meaning: to bring down or abase someone

explanation.walkthrough: In the sullen sense it rhymes with flower; in the humbling sense it rhymes with slower.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to scowl or look threatening, and also to reduce someone's dignity or status.
